messages:
maria: Escalation from AcmeCorp — repeated 5xxs and long-tail latency on /v1/generate starting ~2026-02-14T03:20Z. Customer reports multiple request IDs: req_aa12, req_aa13, req_aa14. They included a curl that times out. Ticket #ACME-12345. Can infra grab pod logs + node metrics and a debug bundle?

josh: ACK. Is this hitting the Dedicated EU cluster (eu-dedicated-2)? Need the exact failing request-id (full header) and the pod name if available.

maria: Customer pasted this minimal repro, they removed sensitive parts but left headers:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_aa12" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}' 
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 502
Body: {"error":"upstream timeout","request_id":"req_aa12"}
Pod name from customer logs: inference-xyz-7f9c.

dana: Thanks — likely upstream timeout from the inference pod or router. Quick checklist to collect repro data (run as redwood-admin or SRE):

1) Pod logs (last 30m, include previous container):
```
kubectl -n dedicated-acme logs deployment/inference-xyz --since=30m > /tmp/inference-xyz.pod.log 2>&1
kubectl -n dedicated-acme logs deployment/inference-xyz -p --since=30m > /tmp/inference-xyz.prev.log 2>&1
```
2) Pod -> Node mapping and container status:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pod inference-xyz-7f9c -o wide > /tmp/inference-xyz.pod.info
kubectl -n dedicated-acme describe pod inference-xyz-7f9c > /tmp/inference-xyz.describe
```
3) Node-level captures (on node gpu-node-eu-22):
```
ssh ubuntu@gpu-node-eu-22 
# dmesg for kernel/Xid, oom, NV driver messages
dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/node.dmesg
# kubelet/journald around the window
sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-02-14 03:00:00" --until "2026-02-14 03:30:00" > /tmp/kubelet.journal
# container runtime logs (containerd)
sudo journalctl -u containerd --since "2026-02-14 03:00:00" > /tmp/containerd.journal
```
4) GPU telemetry sampling (run for ~60s if still reproducing):
```
# nvml query loop sample (requires nvml/nvidia-smi in path)
watch -n 1 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,memory.used,temperature.gpu --format=csv" > /tmp/gpu.sample.csv &
# or one-shot csv for the window
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -lms 1000 -f /tmp/gpu.trace.csv &
```
5) Router / gateway logs (if accessible on router nodes) and trace link: trace id we need: trace:tr-acme-20260214-0312 (if provided).

dana: Also run the support bundle tool for correlation (this collects logs, traces, kernel events):
```
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect_debug_bundle --nodes gpu-node-eu-22 --pods inference-xyz-7f9c --since "2026-02-14T03:10:00Z" --out /tmp/acme-acme-12345-bundle.tar.gz
```
Include the request IDs with the bundle so engineers can fast-filter.

sam: If anyone can't run collect_debug_bundle, I can pull things from the control plane (I have access to cluster snapshots). Also need the image tag of the inference runtime (v2.1.4? confirm). If rollout happened near 03:18 UTC, that might correlate.

josh: I'm on node collection now. First grabbing pod -> node mapping:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pod inference-xyz-7f9c -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}'
# returns: gpu-node-eu-22
```
Starting log grabs and nvml samples, will scp bundle when ready.

infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: "rollout inference-runtime v2.1.4 -> completed (03:18:45 UTC)" :eyes:

maria: Confirmed customer saw spike right after that time. Customer message: "we saw 5 concurrent timeouts between 03:19-03:22 UTC, request IDs: req_aa12, req_aa13, req_aa14".

dana: Priorities for the bundle review:
- correlate router trace IDs to pod logs and GPU samples
- check for Xid/kernels errors in dmesg (NV driver)
- look for OOMKiller entries or repeated container restarts
- check inference runtime logs for model load/unload and KV cache errors

josh: Bundle collected and uploaded: s3://redwood-support-bundles/acme/ACME-12345-2019003456.tar.gz (internal access only). I included nvml CSV + dmesg + pod logs + kubelet journal.

maria: Thanks. I'm sending the bundle and a checklist back to the customer. Also asking them to re-run the same curl with an extra header to capture extended trace if it occurs again: `-H "X-Debug: 1"` so we get the internal trace id in response headers.

sam: I'll start correlating traces and check runtime metrics (latency per-request, queue depth). If we see memory spikes, we'll look at quantization fallback or model reload thrash.

dana: If kernel Xid found, escalate to infra oncall (pager) — kernel GPU Xids typically indicate driver/PCI errors. If only router timeouts, check autoscaler/queued requests.

maria: Customer updated: they ran curl with `X-Debug:1` and returned header `X-Trace-ID: tr-acme-20260214-0319-7f`. Adding that to the bundle note.

josh: Noted. Will annotate the S3 bundle with the trace id and the exact request timestamps.

maria: Great work team :thumbsup: — I'll update ticket ACME-12345 with the S3 link and next steps.
